key_insight: GraphBEAT turns irregular longitudinal EHR events into time-aware graphs, improving early cancer risk stratification with far lower compute than standard deep learning baselines.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help identify patients at higher risk of gastrointestinal cancers earlier using routinely collected diagnosis codes and lab tests.
method: Buckets EHR events over time to handle sparsity and irregular visit timing
Builds patient-specific directed graphs where nodes encode feature, value, and time
Uses time-decay message passing plus multi-head attention pooling for prediction
evidence_signal: Trained and tested on multi-site longitudinal diagnosis codes and laboratory tests, GraphBEAT outperformed GraphSAGE, GAT, GCN, Transformer, and LSTM for pancreatic, liver, and intestinal cancer prediction at 12-, 24-, and 36-month lead times.
watch_item: Performance was shown on retrospective EHR data, so real-world generalization and prospective clinical utility still need validation.
paper_title: GraphBEAT: Graph-based Bucketized Event Aggregation Over Time for Early Risk Stratification of Gastrointestinal Cancers
